issues.description: Element: Animal constructor. The problem statement UML declares a constructor signature Animal(String, int) (name and age) while the provided code (solution and template) defines and uses a single-argument constructor Animal(String). This mismatch leaves students unsure which constructor to implement and whether subclasses and example instantiations should pass an age parameter.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor signature consistent across artifacts. Option A (if age should be taught): update the template and solution to implement Animal(String name, int age), add a private int age field with getter/setter, and update all subclass constructors (Seal, Pig, Goat) and example instantiations in Main to pass an age. Option B (if age is not intended): update the problem statement UML and any textual references to specify Animal(String) only, removing the age parameter from the UML and description. Prefer option A only if the learning objective includes the age attribute; otherwise prefer option B to match existing code.

issues.description: Element: Animal attribute 'age'. The problem statement UML declares two attributes for Animal: name: String and age: int, but the solution's Animal class defines only a private String name and omits any int age field. This structural discrepancy can confuse students about required class state and required getters/setters.
issues.suggestedFix: Either add the missing age attribute to the code or remove it from the UML/text. Option A (add attribute): add private int age to Animal, update the constructor to Animal(String name, int age), add getAge()/setAge(), and update all subclass constructors and example instantiations to provide an age. Option B (remove attribute): edit the problem statement/UML to remove the age attribute and any mention of Animal(String, int), clarifying that Animal only requires a name. Choose the option that matches the intended learning outcome; if the exercise aims to teach attributes beyond name, adopt Option A and update template and solution accordingly.
